$schemaNote: Golden set for scripts/eval-ai.ts (design §9.2). 30 hand-checked Q&A pairs in this app's domain (React, Next.js, TypeScript, Mongoose/MongoDB, Clerk, Tailwind, Zod, Node). Each entry states what a good answer must contain (expectedPoints) — the eval judge scores the draft against these points plus the retrieved sources. Keep points to verifiable facts; never invent library APIs here.

expectedPoints: State updates are asynchronous and scheduled, not applied synchronously
The variable still holds the old value in the same render / event handler
Use the functional update form setState(prev => ...) when the next value depends on the previous one
Use useEffect to react to the new value after the re-render
pairs.question: Why does my React useState value not update immediately after calling the setter?

expectedPoints: Add a loading.tsx file in the route segment folder
Next.js wraps the page in a Suspense boundary automatically
The loading UI shows while the page (or its async data) is loading
loading.tsx must be a React component, default export
pairs.question: How do I show a loading state for a page in the Next.js App Router?

expectedPoints: Server Components are the default and cannot use state, effects, or browser APIs
Add 'use client' at the top of a file that uses useState, useEffect, event handlers, or browser-only APIs
The directive marks the component and its imports as client-rendered
Data fetching and other server-only work should stay in Server Components
pairs.question: When do I need 'use client' in a Next.js App Router component?

expectedPoints: Interfaces can be extended and merged (declaration merging); types cannot be reopened
Types support unions, intersections, tuples and mapped types more directly
Both can describe object shapes and be used for props
Interfaces are generally preferred for object shapes and public APIs, types for unions and utility types
pairs.question: What is the difference between type and interface in TypeScript?

expectedPoints: The schema field must be an ObjectId with a ref to the other model
Call .populate('field') on the query before awaiting it
populate replaces the stored ObjectId with the referenced document
select can limit which fields of the populated document are returned
pairs.question: How do I load referenced documents in Mongoose with populate?

expectedPoints: E11000 means a unique index was violated by the insert or update
unique: true in a schema creates a unique index in MongoDB
The error is thrown by MongoDB, not by Mongoose validation
Handle it by catching the error and checking code 11000, e.g. to report 'already exists'
pairs.question: Why do I get MongoServerError E11000 duplicate key error in Mongoose?

expectedPoints: Import auth from @clerk/nextjs/server and call await auth()
It returns userId (null when signed out) and session claims
Use it in Server Components, Route Handlers and Server Actions
For client components use the useUser or useAuth hooks instead
pairs.question: How do I get the signed-in user in a Next.js Server Component with Clerk?

expectedPoints: Configure darkMode: 'class' in tailwind.config (or the equivalent in CSS-first setups)
Toggle a dark class on the html element to switch themes
Prefix utilities with dark: to apply them only in dark mode
Without the class strategy, dark: follows the OS prefers-color-scheme media query
pairs.question: How does dark mode work with Tailwind CSS class strategy?

expectedPoints: Define a schema with z.object and field validators
Use schema.safeParse(data) which returns { success: true, data } or { success: false, error }
parse() throws on invalid data while safeParse() does not
Errors are ZodIssue objects accessible via error.issues or error.flatten()
pairs.question: How do I validate form data with Zod and handle errors without throwing?

expectedPoints: React StrictMode intentionally mounts, unmounts and remounts effects in development to surface bugs
This only happens in development, not in production builds
Effects should be idempotent and clean up subscriptions, timers and listeners in their return function
Removing StrictMode hides the symptom instead of fixing the effect
pairs.question: Why does my React useEffect run twice in development?

expectedPoints: Call revalidatePath(path) in a Server Action or Route Handler after the mutation
revalidatePath tells Next.js to refetch the data for that route on the next request
revalidateTag(tag) refreshes all cached fetches with that tag
Alternatively use router.refresh() on the client to re-request the current route
pairs.question: How do I refresh server-rendered data after a mutation in Next.js App Router?

expectedPoints: Use the $lookup stage with from, localField, foreignField and as
$lookup adds an array field with the matching documents from the other collection
It runs inside an aggregation pipeline, not a find query
Use $unwind afterwards if you need one document per joined match
pairs.question: How do I join collections in MongoDB with the aggregation pipeline?

expectedPoints: A closure is a function that remembers variables from the scope where it was created
The inner function keeps access to outer variables even after the outer function returns
Common uses: data privacy, factory functions, callbacks and event handlers
Each call to the outer function creates a fresh, independent closure
pairs.question: What is a closure in JavaScript and why is it useful?

expectedPoints: Promise.all rejects as soon as any input promise rejects, and returns results in input order
Promise.allSettled waits for every promise and never rejects
allSettled results are objects with status 'fulfilled' or 'rejected' plus value or reason
Use all when any failure should fail the whole batch, allSettled when partial results are acceptable
pairs.question: What is the difference between Promise.all and Promise.allSettled?

expectedPoints: Keys let React identify which items changed, were added or removed between renders
Keys must be stable and unique among siblings, ideally a database id
Using array indexes as keys breaks when the list is reordered, filtered or items are inserted
Keys are not passed to the component as props
pairs.question: Why does React warn that each child in a list should have a unique key?

expectedPoints: Create a folder named [id] (or [slug]) under app for the dynamic segment
The page receives params as a prop; in recent Next.js versions params is a Promise and must be awaited
Use the param value to load the matching record, e.g. from a database
Call notFound() when no record matches the parameter
pairs.question: How do I read a dynamic route parameter in a Next.js App Router page?

expectedPoints: lean() returns plain JavaScript objects instead of Mongoose documents
Lean queries are faster and use less memory because no document hydration happens
Lean results have no save(), virtuals or getters unless explicitly enabled
Use it for read-only queries; skip it when you need to modify and save the document
pairs.question: What does .lean() do in Mongoose and when should I use it?

expectedPoints: Generics let a function, class or type work with a type parameter (e.g. <T>) instead of a fixed type
The caller supplies the concrete type, or TypeScript infers it from the arguments
They preserve type information through the function instead of falling back to any
Constraints with extends (e.g. <T extends object>) limit which types are allowed
pairs.question: How do generics work in TypeScript?

expectedPoints: Set display: flex on the parent container
justify-content: center centers along the main (horizontal) axis
align-items: center centers along the cross (vertical) axis
The parent needs a height (e.g. min-height: 100vh) for vertical centering to be visible
pairs.question: How do I center a div horizontally and vertically with CSS Flexbox?

expectedPoints: useMemo memoizes a computed value; useCallback memoizes a function reference
Both take a dependency array and recompute only when a dependency changes
Use them to avoid expensive recomputation or to keep stable references for memoized children and effects
Do not wrap everything — memoization itself has a cost and is unnecessary for cheap values
pairs.question: When should I use useMemo versus useCallback in React?

expectedPoints: ES modules use import/export; CommonJS uses require/module.exports
ES modules are statically analyzable and support top-level await; CommonJS loads synchronously at runtime
Node treats .mjs files (or packages with type: module) as ESM and .cjs as CommonJS
Mixing them requires care: require() cannot load ESM and import of CJS gives a default export
pairs.question: What is the difference between ES modules and CommonJS in Node.js?

expectedPoints: An index lets MongoDB find matching documents without scanning the whole collection
A compound index covers multiple fields in one index, in a defined order
Index field order matters: equality fields first, then sort/range fields
Indexes cost write performance and storage, so index only fields you actually query or sort by
pairs.question: How do MongoDB indexes speed up queries and what is a compound index?

expectedPoints: The exported config.matcher lists the paths the middleware runs on
Patterns use path-to-regexp style syntax, e.g. '/((?!_next|.*\\..*).*)'
Requests not matching the pattern skip the middleware entirely
Static files and internals like _next are usually excluded so middleware does not run on every asset
pairs.question: How does the matcher config work in Next.js middleware?

expectedPoints: A controlled input's value comes from React state and updates via onChange
An uncontrolled input keeps its own DOM state and is read via a ref or defaultValue
Controlled inputs give React full control for validation and formatting
Uncontrolled inputs are simpler for one-off reads but harder to validate live
pairs.question: What is the difference between controlled and uncontrolled inputs in React?

expectedPoints: any disables type checking completely; unknown is type-safe
A value of type unknown cannot be used until it is narrowed with a type guard or assertion
unknown is the safe choice for values whose type you genuinely do not know
Prefer unknown plus narrowing over any in all new code
pairs.question: What is the difference between unknown and any in TypeScript?

expectedPoints: Register a schema.pre('save', async function (next) { ... }) hook
Only hash when the password field was modified, using this.isModified('password')
Hash with bcrypt (or argon2) and store the hash, never the plain password
Call next() (or return) so the save continues; handle errors by passing them to next(err)
pairs.question: How do I hash a password before saving a user with a Mongoose pre-save hook?

expectedPoints: JavaScript is single-threaded; async work is scheduled and callbacks run when the call stack is empty
Promise callbacks go to the microtask queue, which runs before the macrotask queue
setTimeout callbacks go to the macrotask queue, so a resolved promise always runs before a 0ms timer
Long synchronous work blocks the event loop and delays all timers and promise callbacks
pairs.question: How does the JavaScript event loop handle promises and setTimeout?

expectedPoints: It automatically optimizes images (resizing, modern formats like WebP/AVIF) at build or request time
It prevents layout shift by requiring width/height or fill sizing
It lazy-loads images outside the viewport by default
Remote images need their domains allow-listed in next.config (images.remotePatterns)
pairs.question: Why should I use the Next.js Image component instead of a plain img tag?

expectedPoints: Context avoids prop drilling when many intermediate components would only forward the value
Typical uses: theme, auth state, locale — data needed by many components at different depths
Every context value change re-renders all consumers, so split contexts or memoize the value
For data that changes often or needs complex updates, a state library is usually a better fit
pairs.question: When should I use React Context instead of passing props down?

expectedPoints: $vectorSearch is the first stage of an aggregation pipeline and finds vectors closest to a query vector
It needs a vector search index on the embedding field, created in Atlas (UI on free/shared tiers)
You pass a queryVector plus numCandidates and limit; results include a vectorSearchScore
Typical RAG flow: embed the question, $vectorSearch top-k chunks, rerank, then pass the excerpts to the LLM as context
pairs.question: How does $vectorSearch work in MongoDB Atlas for retrieval-augmented generation?
